topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes on cancer genetics and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor Viruses and Experimental Models of Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the discovery of oncogenes through tumor virology and detail the laboratory assays used to evaluate cellular transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors in Cell Cycle Regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classes of cancer genes and illustrate how dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations disrupt cell cycle control pathways.

topics.label: Molecular Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation that generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumor Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutation acquisition and inherited genetic defects drive cancer progression and therapeutic evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture with reading recommendations and a preview of the upcoming session.
